items.headline: Gifts and perks to win clients are banned
items.whats_changing: Providers can't give or offer gifts, payments or perks to win or keep participants, including gifts to families or people who refer. Cash, gift cards, alcohol, tobacco and devices are banned in all cases.
items.who_it_affects: Every NDIS provider, registered or unregistered.
items.what_to_do: Remove sign-up gifts, giveaways and referral payments from your marketing before 20 November.

items.headline: Claims must be made within 90 days
items.whats_changing: The time to make a claim for an NDIS support drops from 2 years to 90 days after the support is delivered.
items.who_it_affects: Providers, plan managers and self-managing participants who make NDIS claims.
items.what_to_do: Claim each support soon after you deliver it, and lodge any older claims before 1 December.

items.headline: Price limits rise for 4 household supports
items.whats_changing: Price limits go up for house cleaning, house or yard maintenance, personal domestic activities and specialised home-based assistance for a child.
items.who_it_affects: Providers of these household and home-based supports.
items.what_to_do: Talk to each participant before changing an existing service agreement. They must agree to the new price first.

items.headline: Registration expected to expand to high-risk supports
items.whats_changing: Mandatory registration is set to expand to high-risk supports, such as personal care. It starts in July 2027, with everyone in scope by December 2030. The final list isn't published yet.
items.who_it_affects: Unregistered providers of high-risk supports, such as personal care.
items.what_to_do: If you're unregistered and deliver personal care, start preparing for registration now.
